_note: Complete 61-role Role OS portrait roster (plus 3 specialty deep-audit auditors = 64 entries). Canonical checklist is the route.mjs ROLE_CATALOG (61 distinct roles, the figure the README header cites). The 12 hero roles from Batch 1 are preserved byte-for-byte; the remaining roles were derived from each role's Mission (.claude/agents/**/*.md) or its code contract (artifacts.mjs, packs.mjs, brainstorm-roles.mjs, route.mjs). crew keys house-style.json pack_palette (11 palettes); disposition keys disposition_expression (8). Dispositions are sensible defaults (re-speccable via the dossier). Fields: role, function, specialization, crew, disposition, grade, charter.

judge.charter: Render a final verdict on a synthesized dispute graph — weigh every challenge and rebuttal, then decide accept / expand / re-synthesize / reject. Judges the work, never authors it.

orchestrator.charter: Turn a request into the smallest lawful sequence of role-owned work.

critic-reviewer.charter: Accept, reject, or block work based on contract compliance, quality, and truthfulness.

product-strategist.charter: Shape work so it solves the real product problem without scope drift or thesis loss.

security-reviewer.charter: Review code and configuration for security vulnerabilities — injection, auth gaps, secret exposure, unsafe defaults, OWASP top 10.

backend-engineer.charter: Implement reliable server-side behavior, data flow, and system contracts needed for the product outcome.

ux-researcher.charter: Identify user friction, flow pain, and usability issues through evidence — observed behavior and structured analysis, not opinion.

launch-copywriter.charter: Turn completed product value into clear, credible launch messaging without hype or invention.

release-engineer.charter: Prepare and execute clean releases — versioning, changelog, packaging, tagging, publish readiness — so shipped artifacts are correct and traceable.

component-auditor.charter: Read every line in an assigned code component and produce structured findings for every material issue.

brand-guardian.charter: Protect product identity — tone, terminology, visual language, fiction consistency — across all surfaces, preventing drift.

contrarian-analyst.charter: Challenge specific claims by ID — expose overstatement, contradiction, and structural flaws; never generate, only refute.

ui-designer.charter: Design the screen structure and interaction approach that best expresses the intended product behavior.

frontend-developer.charter: Implement user-facing interfaces and interactions faithfully, cleanly, and in line with project conventions.

test-engineer.charter: Verify that the work is defended against regression, edge cases, and false confidence.

performance-engineer.charter: Identify and fix performance problems using measurement, not intuition — hot paths, regressions, memory leaks, and budget violations.

refactor-engineer.charter: Improve code structure without changing behavior — reduce complexity, eliminate duplication, clarify boundaries, and improve maintainability.

dependency-auditor.charter: Assess dependency health — stale packages, known vulnerabilities, supply-chain risk, unnecessary bloat, and version drift.

repo-researcher.charter: Map the live truth of a repository — structure, entrypoints, seams, build paths, and runtime shape — so downstream roles work from verified fact, not stale assumptions.

repo-translator.charter: Translate documentation across languages and audiences faithfully, preserving technical accuracy and product voice without invention.

docs-architect.charter: Design information structure and build searchable, navigable documentation — owning both the hierarchy and the docs artifact itself.

metadata-curator.charter: Ensure repository metadata, package manifests, and discovery surfaces are accurate, complete, and consistent with the product's actual state.

coverage-auditor.charter: Assess test coverage truthfully — what is proven, what is unproven, where false confidence exists — and recommend targeted improvements.

deployment-verifier.charter: Verify that deployed artifacts actually work — landing pages render, packages install, docs are searchable, badges resolve, and live surfaces match what was shipped.

launch-strategist.charter: Plan launches so they reach the right audience with the right proof at the right time — without hype, invented metrics, or premature claims.

content-strategist.charter: Plan long-form content that bridges documentation and marketing — technical articles, announcement angles, case studies, and docs-to-audience pipelines.

community-manager.charter: Manage community interactions — issues, discussions, contributions, and feedback loops — with responsiveness and honesty, without hype or false promises.

support-triage-lead.charter: Classify and route incoming support requests efficiently — separating bugs from feature requests, user errors from product failures, and urgent from routine.

feedback-synthesizer.charter: Turn scattered user signals — issues, complaints, feature requests, usage patterns — into actionable product insights without inflation or invention.

roadmap-prioritizer.charter: Sequence work by leverage, risk, and dependency truth — not by loudness, recency, or wishful thinking.

spec-writer.charter: Turn ambiguous goals into execution-grade specifications that downstream roles can implement without guessing.

competitive-analyst.charter: Map the competitive landscape truthfully — what alternatives exist, where they're strong, where they're weak, and what differentiation actually holds.

trend-researcher.charter: Identify relevant technical, market, and ecosystem trends that could affect product decisions — without hype, speculation, or trend-chasing.

user-interview-synthesizer.charter: Extract actionable insights from user interviews — patterns, unmet needs, mental models, and priority signals — without projecting desired outcomes onto user words.

context-scout.charter: Map the surrounding domain — terminology, adjacent spaces, and prior art — so exploration is grounded in what already exists.

user-value-scout.charter: Surface where the felt pull and pain live — user pains, unmet needs, and desire signals across segments.

creative-leap-scout.charter: Generate bold, unexpected directions through cross-domain analogy and novel combination — the divergent lens against sameness.

normalizer.charter: Translate role-native outputs into provenance-preserving claim atoms — deduplicate, detect conflicts, and calibrate evidence without flattening source identity.

synthesizer.charter: Synthesize a real dispute graph into a bounded set of advancing directions, each cited to truth-layer atoms, preserving tensions rather than collapsing them.

product-expander.charter: Expand a synthesis direction into a concrete product shape — target user, core mechanism, features, core loop, and smallest proof.

mechanics-scout.charter: Probe how a direction actually works — the operational mechanisms and structural feasibility that have to hold for it to be real.

market-scout.charter: Locate market whitespace and existing solutions — where the sameness trap lies and where genuine positioning room remains.

contrarian-scout.charter: Challenge findings and evidence — expose overgeneralization, false novelty, and weak support before they harden into direction.

feasibility-scout.charter: Assess whether a direction is feasible and provable — buildability, complexity, and a realistic proof timeline.

quality-bar-scout.charter: Set the bar for excellence — define what an adequate versus exceptional version of a direction must clear.

scenario-expander.charter: Ground a concept in concrete user scenarios — situations, edge cases, and failure modes that test whether it holds up in use.

moat-expander.charter: Analyze defensibility — stickiness, competitive moat, and phase planning that keep a direction defensible over time.

context-analyst.charter: Map what something is, what it sits next to, and what it is not — terminology genealogy, adjacency, and category boundaries, never user desire or positioning.

user-value-analyst.charter: Locate the felt pull and pain — jobs-to-be-done, frictions, unmet desires, and willingness signals, never mechanism or competitive framing.

mechanics-analyst.charter: Determine what must be true for a direction to work — loop decomposition, dependency chains, and failure modes, never messaging or user willingness.

positioning-analyst.charter: Identify what claim a direction could own and when it is legal to make it — substitutes, wedge candidates, and category frame, never implementation.

test-truth-auditor.charter: Distinguish tests that prove behavior from tests that merely exist — name untested-but-risky paths, ceremonial tests, and integration gaps, and estimate real coverage.

seam-auditor.charter: Inspect every declared boundary from the dependency graph — surface false-independence risks, content-code drift, and wrong dependency direction across components.

audit-synthesizer.charter: Reconcile findings across all audit parcels into a ranked verdict, adjudicate contradictions, and produce an action plan grouped by root cause and leverage.

swarm-coordinator.charter: Evaluate exit conditions against accumulated wave findings and decide loop / advance / halt — gating each convergence stage on build results and user approval.

swarm-backend-agent.charter: Inspect every file in the backend domain, severity-triage findings, and apply remediations in order until the build passes — within exclusive file ownership.

swarm-bridge-agent.charter: Inspect every file in the integration / bridge domain, severity-triage findings, and apply remediations until the build passes — within exclusive file ownership.

swarm-tests-agent.charter: Audit the test suite for gaps, ceremonial tests, and fixture quality, report coverage delta, and apply fixes until the build passes — within exclusive file ownership.

swarm-infra-agent.charter: Inspect CI workflows, config files, and docs, severity-triage findings, and apply remediations until the build passes — within exclusive file ownership.

swarm-frontend-agent.charter: Audit the UI layer for bugs, accessibility, and UX, list accessibility issues separately, and apply fixes until the build passes — within exclusive file ownership.

swarm-synthesizer.charter: Summarize all swarm stages, tally findings fixed versus remaining, run the final test suite, and recommend ship, hold, or re-swarm.

red-teamer.charter: Attempt to break a subject under test across many attack vectors, compute a catch rate, itemize uncaught breaks with reproductions, and flag pipelines that reject 0/N attacks as suspect.

caption-auditor.charter: Audit a captioned dataset against its rules — compute per-rule compliance over a declared sample, cite each violation by record id, and refuse to PASS on tiny samples claiming perfection.

monster-taxonomy-verifier.charter: Verify monster taxonomy entries against schema — compute per-field compliance, enumerate missing fields, declare LoRA-separability explicitly, and flag human-element contamination in pure-monster scope.
